laws.def: In force since February 2, 2025, with fines to €35M or 7% of global turnover. Prohibits AI that manipulates or exploits vulnerability into significant psychological or financial harm — Commission guidance explicitly cites products promising unrealistic mental-health benefits.
laws.sub: Our answer: Guardrails refuse health, death, pregnancy, and specific financial predictions by design.

laws.def: Effective January 1, 2026. Where a reasonable person could believe they're talking to a human, operators must give clear and conspicuous notice that it's AI, maintain self-harm protocols — and face a private right of action.
laws.sub: Our answer: AI-disclosure by default; Attest makes the human/AI boundary explicit and provable.

laws.def: AI Companion Models statute, effective November 5, 2025. Disclosure duties and safety protocols for AI companions; Utah and Maine moved the same year. Expect ten-plus states and a likely FTC rule by ~2030.
laws.sub: Our answer: the human-vs-AI distinction becomes a legal requirement — which makes verified-human attestation a compliance feature, not a slogan.

laws.def: Running since September 2024: DoNotPay's “robot lawyer” settled, Workado's accuracy claims prosecuted. The posture: existing deception law applies to AI, no differently. The FTC and state AGs also have a long history against fraudulent psychic operations.
laws.sub: Our answer: truthful “read by a human” labeling is precisely the claim the FTC rewards — because we can prove it.

laws.def: Groups fortune-telling with spam; astrology apps report serial rejections (Struck: roughly ten). A white-label vendor shipping hundreds of near-identical practitioner apps would be a mass-rejection machine.
laws.sub: Our answer: web-first, PWA-first distribution with differentiated practitioner branding — and IAP-compliant checkout where stores are unavoidable.

laws.def: “Psychic services and fortune tellers” sit on the restricted list — prior written approval, jurisdiction bans, and practitioners report cancellations for the words on their checkout page.
laws.sub: Our answer: high-risk / merchant-of-record rails, careful category coding, conservative chargeback controls — with the Guardrails layer as underwriting evidence.

laws.def: Ads may not assert or imply a viewer's religion, health, or emotional state — sharply constraining “you”-style spiritual ad copy, with enforcement increasingly AI-driven and proactive.
laws.sub: Our answer: compliant, benefit-focused ad templates ship with every storefront.

guardrails.name: Hard refusals
guardrails.blurb: No health prognoses, no death predictions, no pregnancy calls, no specific financial picks. These aren't product decisions to revisit — they're constitutional.

guardrails.name: Disclosure by default
guardrails.blurb: Every AI-assisted artifact says so, plainly, before a seeker reads a word. SB 243's “clear and conspicuous” standard is our floor, not our ceiling.

guardrails.name: Crisis protocols
guardrails.blurb: Self-harm signal detection routes to crisis resources and pauses the session — mandated in California and New York, active everywhere we operate.

guardrails.name: Audit trail
guardrails.blurb: Guardrail events, disclosures, and attestations are logged and exportable — the underwriting evidence that gets a practitioner through high-risk payments review.
